answer: Clones grown from one prompt kernel share an accent that shows across hundreds of answers. Every 20 epochs (assumed), the protocol compresses each seat's answer history alone, then zipped together with each other seat's. If two histories shrink far more together than apart (normalized compression distance under 0.6, assumed), they hang from one vine and get pooled into one paid seat. Agents split by a canyon of different models and habits barely compress together, so they keep full pay.
